events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Guam Coastal Waters; Rota Coastal Waters
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...West winds 15 to 25 kt with gusts up to 35 kt and seas
8 to 11 feet.

* WHERE...Guam and Rota Coastal Waters.

* WHEN...Until 5 AM ChST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Moderate to strong westerlies prevail
across the Marianas as another resurgence in the monsoon builds
over the northern CNMI, likely to maintain moderate to strong
winds through the middle of next week, with the strongest winds
expected over Tinian and Saipan waters. Combined seas of 8 to 11
feet are expected over the next few days, remaining hazardous
to small craft through at least early Tuesday morning, and the
Small Craft Advisory was extended until 5 AM ChST Tuesday. Seas
look to fall below hazardous levels for Guam and Rota by midweek
as swells and wind waves relax.

events.region: Tinian Coastal Waters; Saipan Coastal Waters
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...West winds 15 to 25 kt with gusts up to 35 kt and seas
8 to 11 feet.

* WHERE...Tinian and Saipan Coastal Waters.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM ChST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Moderate to strong westerlies prevail
across the Marianas as another resurgence in the monsoon builds
over the northern CNMI, likely to maintain moderate to strong
winds through the middle of next week over Tinian and Saipan
waters. Combined seas of 8 to 11 feet are expected to continue
through much of the coming week, remaining hazardous to small
craft through at least Thursday afternoon as the southern edge
of the monsoon surge persists overhead. So, the Small Craft
Advisory was extended for Tinian and Saipan waters through 5 PM
ChST Thursday.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Hazardous surf of 7 to 10 ft.

* WHERE...North facing reefs of Yap.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM ChST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Long-period swell, originating from
distant Typhoon Dolphin, is still expected to bring hazardous
surf along north-facing reefs through much of the weekend. As
swells diminish, surf is expected to subside below hazardous
levels of 9 feet by Sunday night.
